name: PT ABM Investama Tbk

frontmatter.title: ABM Investama — the parts are worth more, the discount is what you own
frontmatter.summary: ABMM is a family-controlled holding whose listed GEMS stake and contractor, logistics and fabrication arms are worth more than the price. We accept the review: the re-rating cross-checks are dropped, MDB is marked at its transaction value, and the market's discount is held. The parts and the dividend support ADD.
thesis: The market prices ABMM as a thermal-coal producer; on the audited numbers it is a holding company whose listed GEMS associate is the largest part and whose contractor, logistics and fabrication businesses earn fees.
The data pack understates depreciation by an order of magnitude; we restate D&A from the audited notes and mark the operating segments on the LTM to 30 September 2026.
The discount is the base rate: the base holds the discount the market applies and assumes no narrowing, so the mechanical roll and the dividend, not a re-rating, support the rating.

PJU's and NCN's reserves are disclosed; the group's own coal transactions value reserves at the low end, so the development mine is carried at acquisition fair value and reserve upside is the bull's option.
Related-party revenue, the MDB transfer below book and the concentrated register warrant a discount above the peer modal level.

catalysts.event: PT Piranti Jaya Utama first cut targeted in Central Kalimantan; Aceh production continues to ramp
FY2026 audited results and dividend declaration
IDX minimum free-float step due: fifteen per cent required and the registry is just below it
Aceh (NCN) IUP renewal window and Central Kalimantan permitting milestones

blocks.text: We move ABM Investama (ABMM) to ADD from BUY with a twelve-month target of Rp2,621 against a last price of Rp2,540 — an expected total return of 11.0% including the Rp198 next-twelve-month dividend [S0, S12]. The review was right that the prior BUY rested on a re-rating; we removed it. Valuation is now the parts alone. The own-history P/E and P/BV legs are dropped, not down-weighted: both were struck on five-year average multiples while the market today pays 2.7x earnings and 0.4x book, so the old blend assumed a discount narrowing in a base that said it persists [S0]. At the discount the market actually applies, the parts equal the price. The target from there is mechanical: each scenario value is compounded one year at the 20.3% cost of equity and reduced by the Rp198 next-twelve-month dividend, the scenarios are probability-weighted, and the 10.0% liquidity discount is applied. The 11.0% expected return is therefore 7.8% of dividend yield plus a 3.2% roll of a static market mark at the cost of equity, not carry on the operating business [S0].

What changed is the evidence. The SOTP now deducts the 30 September 2026 net debt, carries MDB at the only observable transaction value, and marks the operating segments on the twelve months to 30 September 2026 [S15, S5]. We charge holdco overhead as a separate ten-times line and correct the claim that PJU's reserves are not disclosed: they are, and so are NCN's [S8].

ABMM is an integrated energy group in the Tiara Marga Trakindo group: contractor, logistics and sea transport, fabrication, fuel trading, three coal concessions and associates [S4, S8]. Its own coal sales are immaterial: the historic South Kalimantan mine's reserves were "fully depleted as of the end of December 2024" and it sold 0.3 Mt from that mine in FY2025 [S8]. What it owns is the contracting platform and above all a 30.0% associate stake in the listed PT Golden Energy Mines (GEMS) plus a remaining interest in the unlisted PT Media Djaya Bersama (MDB) [S12, S5]. The GEMS mark alone is worth more than ABMM's entire market capitalisation [S12, S0].

Three things move the value. The GEMS mark is the largest driver, and a fifth off it is the largest single downside in section five [S12]. The holdco discount: today's price implies 68.9% to the corrected pre-discount NAV, and the base applies the same 68.9% [S0]; persistence is the most-likely path, with dated narrowing events in the bull [S13]. Operating EBITDA is marked on the LTM after recurring SG&A [S12].

The base is the most likely path, not the cautious one: volumes and margins are held at the LTM actual, the GEMS mark is the market's own, and the operating parts are marked at comp-supported multiples on true EBITDA. Scenarios flex the discount and GEMS mark; coal and related-party exposure is stated, not double-counted. No third-party ratings, price objectives or published estimates were sought or used.

ABM Investama is an Indonesian integrated energy holding in the Tiara Marga Trakindo group, organised across Mining Value Chain and Logistics, Engineering and New Businesses [S4, S8]. Its operating subsidiaries include PT Cipta Kridatama (contractor), PT Cipta Krida Bahari (logistics), PT Sanggar Sarana Baja (fabrication), PT Reswara Minergi Hartama (coal) and PT Prima Wiguna Parama (fuel trading) [S12]. The mix is why the coal-producer label is wrong: in FY2025 Mining Contractors and Coal Mining contributed US$755.7m of external revenue, Services US$185.2m, Manufacturing US$31.7m and Other US$66.2m [S12, F9]. Contractor and services earn fees; coal reaches revenue only through owner-mined and traded tonnes.

On coal, Reswara owns three mines [S8]. PT Tunas Inti Abadi (TIA), the historic South Kalimantan producer, is fully depleted from the end of 2024; it sold 0.3 Mt in FY2025 of a 4,200 kcal/kg adb coal for domestic power and Chinese blending [S8, S5]. PT Nirmala Coal Nusantara (NCN) in West Aceh holds 31.0 Mt of low-calorie 3,000 kcal/kg GAR coal, its IUP runs to October 23, 2027 and extends once, and it sold 0.4 Mt in 1H2026 [S2, S5, S8]. PT Piranti Jaya Utama (PJU) in Central Kalimantan holds 34.1 Mt of reserves on a 4,800 hectares concession, targets its first cut for the end of 2026, and carries US$56.3m of mining properties recognised on acquisition [S3, S5, S8]. The PJU estimate runs July 2011 to May 2012 per the PT NRM Konsultan Indonesia report of 30 June 2024; the IUP runs to 28 December 2032 [S8].

The associate portfolio is what the coal frame misses. ABMM holds 30.0% of listed GEMS through PT Radhika Jananta Raya, carried at US$488.3m at FY2025 year-end; GEMS earned US$259.8m in FY2025 [S12]. It also holds the unlisted MDB after the April 2026 transfer of a 10.0% stake to PT Inti Murni Kencana for US$10.0m [S5]; the SOTP marks MDB at that transaction value rather than at the US$82.5m book (section four). The customer base, though, is heavily related-party — a mid-sized challenger whose integrated-services platform is built around the group's own mines and third-party clients [S12].

Indonesian thermal coal sits between a seaborne price held up by a war premium and supply discipline, and a domestic framework that taxes exports and caps power-sector prices [S2, S4]. The house coal deck carries a long-run Newcastle marker below spot, and the low-calorie Indonesian index trades at a wide discount to the seaborne benchmark through 1H2026 [S2]. For ABMM coal is second-order: it sets the GEMS value and the small owner-mined tonnes, while the contractor and services books are priced off mining activity and cost per bank cubic metre [S12, S8].

Regulation binds the coal assets. An IUP exploitation permit pays a production royalty that depends on calorific value and the reference coal price, a regime reworked by Government Regulation No. 26 of 2022 and again by Government Regulation No. 19 of 2025, discussed in the filings as a change to the open-pit royalty schedule [S5, S8]. The low-calorie Aceh product sits in the lower tranche, which is why grade matters to the coal-card value [S5, S8]. A domestic market obligation reserves a share of output for the power sector at a capped price [S8].

The contractor landscape is a small set of large players competing on cost per bank cubic metre and delivery reliability [S3, S4]. ABMM competes on integration — pit to mother vessel inside its own ecosystem — and on a long South Kalimantan record [S4]; disclosed on-time and in-full rates are the operating proxies [S4]. On coal it is a price-taker selling a discount product [S8]. The moat is thinner than the integrated narrative: the concessions are finite, the South Kalimantan reserve base is exhausted, and contractor margins depend on renewals at related-party and third-party mines [S12, S8]. Buyer power is high because the customer base is concentrated and related-party, which guarantees volume but weakens the claim that earnings are independently negotiated [S12].

The holding-company regime sets the discount. The exchange staged the minimum free float at fifteen per cent; the registry puts ABMM at 14.97 per cent, just below the line, with the step due 31 March 2027 and the registry marking the company non-compliant [S13, S0]. The step is therefore a live, dated event — the narrowing catalyst in the bull — and a placement to close the gap at a discount remains a per-share leak. We assume neither, and no index re-inclusion.

The reported financials are straightforward once depreciation is corrected. Group revenue fell to US$1,038.2m in FY2025 from US$1,200.1m on lower coal prices and volumes. The 9M2026 LK changes that: revenue US$818.5m, 4.7% higher year on year, gross profit US$98.3m and net profit to parent US$102.3m, 141.4% higher [S15, S16], on lower rainfall hours, higher overburden removal and coal getting, and a lower cost-to-revenue ratio in mining contracting [S16]. The pack's FY2025 depreciation is a fraction of the audited charge; we restate from the notes and build on that [S0, S12, F17].

The restated charge is an order of magnitude larger than the pack's: US$211.6m in FY2025 against US$205.1m in FY2024, across the four segments, with right-of-use and mining-property amortisation inside it [S12, S8]. The company's own EBITDA before associates was US$266.2m; adjusted EBITDA including associates was US$339.3m [S8, S4]. Our operating EBITDA, US$254.2m, excludes other income and associate income and reproduces the FY2025 margin of 24.5% [S0, S12].

The associate stream is the economic core and is missing from the pack's EBITDA. Share of associates' profit was US$84.7m in FY2025, US$58.6m in 1H2026 and US$97.5m in 9M2026 [S12, S5, S15]. Net income rose even though a US$15.8m one-off disposal loss ran through 9M2026 [S15]. For a holdco, cash upstreamed is the test: dividends from associates were US$63.0m in FY2025 against a payout of 21.2% and finance charges of US$76.6m [S12], so the parent is not funding its distribution from asset sales or new debt.

Margins are thin at the operating level and flattered by the D&A add-back. FY2025 gross margin was 10.0%; the LTM to 30 September 2026 is 13.1%, with 9M2026 gross profit of US$98.3m on US$818.5m [S15, S16]. The LTM SG&A carries a one-off expected-credit-loss provision of US$12.0m against a small 9M2025 base, so the forecast uses the recurring ratio of 5.1%; the provision is a receivables write-down, not an operating cost, and the prior-year base charge stays in [S15, F90]. FY2026E revenue is US$1,075.0m, EBITDA US$305.3m, net profit to parent US$141.7m, EPS US$0.0515 and DPS US$0.0109 [S0, S15]. That is the LTM rolled forward: the 3.6% growth, 13.1% margin and 12.6% tax rate are LTM figures, and FY2027 onward is flat [S15, S16]. The DPS applies the last-actual payout ratio to rolled EPS, not a company guide; the trailing payment is Rp97, and a higher payout would need the board to hold the ratio on higher earnings [S0, S8].

Other income is the line that flatters the forecast. 9M2026 other income, net was US$30.7m against US$15.1m a year earlier; the note splits it into US$21.4m of foreign-exchange gain, US$4.5m of fixed-asset disposal gains and US$5.2m of hauling-road revenue, the only clearly recurring stream [S15]. FX gains have recurred in both periods and are partly the mirror of the dollar-reporting, rupiah-cost base; the disposal gains are not recurring. The model holds the LTM figure flat, so both sit in FY2026E net profit of US$141.7m and in the Rp198 dividend that carries the target. If the FX and disposal gains were excluded and the payout held, DPS would fall by roughly a fifth and the total return from 11.0% to a little under ten per cent — still positive, but no longer the whole case [S15, S0].

Cash conversion is the brightest part of the picture. Operating cash flow was US$296.1m in FY2025 against net profit of US$70.6m, and US$204.8m in 9M2026 against a much larger profit, so the accruals ratio stays negative and earnings are not running ahead of cash [S12, S15]. Receivables did not outgrow revenue and inventory fell [S12]. The one quality flag is related-party gravity: 59.1% of FY2025 revenue came from related parties and related-party trade receivables were US$121.7m, a majority of the book [S12]. The GEMS-controlled mines are the largest block, led by PT Borneo Indobara's US$298.7m — contractor work for the associate that anchors the NAV [S12]. Audited and disclosed, it is optics-class, not manipulation-class, but it justifies the wider discount [S12].

Capex is heavy and the balance sheet is levered but manageable. The model carries US$136.6m of FY2025 capex, about 13.2% of revenue [S0, S12]. Net debt was US$766.7m at FY2025, about 3.0x restated EBITDA, and the group refinanced in December 2025 with IDR4.20tn of syndicated facilities plus an accordion [S10, S12]. At 30 September 2026 the LK's own net-debt note puts net debt at US$640.2m — short- and long-term bank loans and lease liabilities less cash of US$220.3m — and the SOTP adds the US$3.3m current and US$8.5m non-current other long-term loans that the note excludes, so the deducted figure is the LK line plus those loans, not the forecast [S15, pp.6, 139, F88, F89]. Equity was US$874.7m at FY2025 and US$957.0m at 30 September 2026, so book value per share is well above the market price [S0, S15].

The dividend has fallen for four years to Rp97 trailing, a 21.2% payout, and family control means policy reflects the controlling shareholder's cash needs [S0, S8]. The group spent the cycle buying mines — NCN in 2024, PJU in 2025 — rather than buying back stock or clearing debt, a defensible growth choice that leaves minorities with illiquid assets [S5, S8]. There is no manipulation-class finding: KAP Purwanto Susanti dan Surja, an Ernst & Young member firm, signed an unqualified FY2025 opinion with no auditor down-tier and no controlling-share pledge [S12, S8].

We value ABMM on the house holdco frame: a sum of the parts with GEMS at market, the operating segments on LTM earnings, MDB at the observable transaction, PJU at acquisition fair value, and 30 September 2026 consolidated net debt deducted once, after parent overhead capitalised at ten times [S12, S15]. The coal-producer life-of-asset DCF is retired [S12]. P/E and P/BV are a cross-check only: they use five-year averages while the market pays 2.7x and 0.4x, so carrying them imported a re-rating [S0].

Cost of equity is 20.3%, from the US risk-free rate, mature-market plus Indonesia country premium, and a levered beta of 2.30; WACC 10.4% [S0]. The twelve-month target adds one year of cost of equity [S0].

GEMS is the largest component, a 30.0% stake at its own market price [S12]. The operating segments are marked on the LTM to 30 September 2026, not FY2025: the segment note gives gross profit and depreciation for both nine-month periods, so LTM segment EBITDA is the FY2025 audited column less the 9M2025 comparative plus the 9M2026 actual, and the four net marks plus elimination sum to LTM gross profit less recurring SG&A before professional fees plus LTM D&A [S12, S15]. That is the last actual and most-likely anchor; FY2025 was already beaten [S16]. Recurring SG&A is allocated pro rata to external revenue. Contractor and coal is at four times net segment EBITDA, inside the mining-services range (KKGI), with a related-party haircut because the GEMS-controlled mines are its largest customers [S12, F61]; services four times, manufacturing three and a half, fuel trading two [S12].

MDB is at the only observable price: the April 2026 transfer of a 10.0% stake to PT Inti Murni Kencana for US$10.0m values the remaining two-fifths at four times that amount [S5, F38, F54]. Book of US$82.5m is not used because it is about twice that value; the US$15.8m disposal loss is the same transaction, making the observable price the mark's upper bound [S15, F78]. PJU is at its US$56.3m acquisition fair value. Its reserves are disclosed: 34.1 Mt of higher-calorie coal (4,600 kcal/kg GAR product) on a 4,800 hectares concession with an IUP to 28 December 2032, from a 2011-2012-vintage estimate, while NCN's 31.0 Mt came with the 2024 acquisition at a much lower value per reserve tonne [S8, F83, F84]. With no mine plan and a fourteen-year-old estimate, its own acquisition price — at the top of its range — is the most-likely mark; reserve upside is the bull's option [S8].

Professional fees are the identifiable parent-level corporate, listing, audit, legal and treasury block, capitalised at ten times on the LTM value and deducted as its own line; the segment marks exclude them so the cost is not multiplied twice [S12, S15, F85-F87]. Consolidated net debt is the 30 September 2026 LK figure: the capital-management note puts net debts at US$640.2m, being short- and long-term bank loans and lease liabilities less cash of US$220.3m, and the SOTP adds the US$3.3m current and US$8.5m non-current other long-term loans that the note excludes — so the deducted net debt is the LK's own line plus those loans [S15, pp.6, 139, F88, F89]. The US$6.1m non-controlling interest is deducted separately [S15, F73].

The base applies a 68.9% discount to pre-discount NAV, giving Rp2,540 per share [S0]. That is the market's own level — the reverse solve prints 68.9% — and it is held flat: the base assumes no narrowing. Because the discount is the market's, the SOTP leg is a market mark; the independent content is the NAV and scenarios. The old presentation compared undiscounted cross-checks with a discounted SOTP; on a comparable basis today's spot multiples equal the price [S0]. The blend's effective discount is the same 68.9%, with no re-rating embedded.

Sensitivity is dominated by the discount: ten points moves the SOTP by close to thirty percent, and the discount is what the catalysts would move. GEMS and segment marks are fixed in the engine, so the scenarios flex the discount and map the GEMS shock into it [S0].

We translate at the macro spot of Rp18,140/USD rather than the FY2027E Rp18,350/USD, slightly conservative for a dollar NAV [S0]. The roll-forward is mechanical and disclosed: each scenario value is compounded one year at the 20.3% cost of equity and reduced by the Rp198 next-twelve-month dividend, the three are probability-weighted, and the 10.0% liquidity discount is applied, giving Rp2,621 [S0]. The 11.0% total return is the 7.8% dividend yield plus the 3.2% roll of a static market mark at the cost of equity. The discount is wider than the peer modal (ADRO, BRPT, CUAN, DSSA and TOBA at thirty percent; ASII at a quarter) because those are larger and index-eligible, while here the controller holds 53.6%, related-party revenue is 59.1%, the float is 14.97 per cent against a fifteen per cent step due 31 March 2027, and a 10.0% MDB stake went to a related party below carrying [S12, S5, S13]. IMJS, a debt-heavy holdco, is at sixty percent; governance warrants the wider end.

The largest downside is the GEMS mark: a thermal-coal producer whose market value and dividend fall with the seaborne price, taking the largest part of ABMM's NAV directly [S12, F47]. The prior draft sized it only in prose. The engine cannot re-price a listed holding inside a scenario, so the bear's twenty per cent GEMS de-rating is mapped into the discount: the de-rating alone is about an eighth of NAV, and the mapped bear value is Rp1,530, below the price [S0]. The same coal price hits the GEMS-controlled mines that supply the contractor's largest related-party block, PT Borneo Indobara alone at US$298.7m of revenue, so the two largest NAV components are correlated [S12, F61]. Likelihood medium, impact high.

The discount: the base assumes persistence at the market's implied level; the bear widens ten points and the bull narrows ten. A widening — from a related-party transaction reminding minority holders why it exists, or a discounted placement — takes value toward the bear [S13, S12]. Holdco discounts persist by default and "it trades below SOTP" is not a thesis; the base is persistence plus the mechanical roll and the dividend, and the catalysts are the bull case [S13].

Governance and related-party gravity, detailed in section six, is the third cluster. Related-party revenue is 59.1% and the largest counterparties are the GEMS-controlled mines, which supplied US$298.7m, US$40.7m and US$31.8m [S12]. The contractor mark is therefore substantially a transfer price with the same associate that anchors the NAV. A repricing or insourcing is the modal IDX value-destruction channel; the contractor multiple carries a haircut, and a repeat related-party transfer at or below the MDB mark is a further downside not modelled because MDB is already at the observable price [S12, F38, F54].

The free-float regime: the registry puts the float at 14.97 per cent, just below the fifteen per cent step due 31 March 2027, so both halves are live — a placement to close the gap at a discount, and the step itself as the bull's dated narrowing event [S13, S0, S8]. We assume neither; no index re-inclusion either; average daily traded value is below the house liquidity threshold, hence the 10.0% discount [S0].

Financial and operational: net debt of US$766.7m at 3.0x restated EBITDA is manageable but not comfortable in a trough, and a rupiah-linked cost base with dollar reporting creates translation drag [S0, S12]. The group depends on contractor contracts at related-party and third-party mines and on two new mines ramping on schedule; a PJU delay or client loss would hit services [S3, S5]. NCN sold 0.4 Mt in 1H2026 and PJU's first cut targets end-2026, leaving little room for slippage [S2, S3, S5]. PJU is at acquisition fair value, not project value; the reserve base is real but the mine plan is not [S5, S8].

The base, bear and bull shock the discount and GEMS by mirrored amounts; all values are before the 10.0% liquidity discount. Base is persistence with a probability-weighted value of Rp2,913 against Rp2,540; the bear de-rates GEMS to Rp1,643 and the bull re-rates to Rp4,293 [S0]. The bear is now an absolute loss, so the downside the section leads with carries probability weight.

Signposts: the PJU first cut on time, the fifteen per cent float step closed by 31 March 2027, or a higher FY2026 dividend upstream would move us toward the bull [S13, S3, S5]. A discounted placement, a further related-party transfer below carrying, a repricing or insourcing of GEMS-controlled contractor revenue, or a GEMS dividend cut would move us toward the bear regardless of coal [S13, S12]. A sustained Newcastle print below the deck's through-cycle marker for more than two quarters would hit the GEMS mark and upstream cash together [S0, S12]. The coal-getting recovery — 8.6 Mt in 1Q2026 after double-digit second-half growth — has begun to reach revenue; a durable turn lifts the segment marks [S4, S3, S15].

Ownership is concentrated and family-anchored. PT Tiara Marga Trakindo holds 53.6%, Valle Verde Pte. Ltd. holds 25.5% and Lo Kheng Hong holds 5.6%; the Hamami family is the ultimate beneficial owner [S8]. The board is led by Achmad Ananda Djajanegara (president director) and Hans Manoe (finance director), with Rachmat Mulyana Hamami as president commissioner [S8]. A RUPSLB on 15 October 2026 gave effect to Haris Mustarto's resignation; the president and finance directors are unchanged and any replacement is not named [S14]. No dividend, new debt, rights issue, placement or other action bearing on the share count or valuation bridge was on that agenda [S14]. No controlling-share pledge is disclosed; loan collateral is bank accounts, receivables, insurance claims and machinery, not the GEMS shares [S12, S8].

Related-party dealings are present, material and disclosed. The group buys equipment, spares and services from Trakindo Utama and other TMT entities, sells contractor services to the GEMS-controlled mines and PT Multi Harapan Utama, and earns associate income from MIFA and GEMS; the related-party share of revenue was 59.1% in FY2025 and related-party trade receivables were US$121.7m [S12]. It also moved a fabrication stake between its own entities and transferred a 10.0% MDB stake to PT Inti Murni Kencana for US$10.0m in April 2026 [S8, S5]. Disclosed and audited, these are optics-class rather than manipulation-class, but they are the discount's DNA [S12].

On ESG the disclosures are typical of an Indonesian integrated miner: solar capacity at a contractor site, a biogas plant in South Kalimantan with carbon-credit recognition, and community-education and operator-development programmes [S3, S4]. The material exposures are environmental and social at the mine sites — dust, water and land rehabilitation at two new concessions — and the governance exposure of a concentrated register [S4, S8].

The dated catalysts are the two new mines and the next disclosures. PJU's first cut targets end-2026 and Aceh should keep ramping after its first 2026 sales [S3, S5]. FY2026 audited results and the dividend declaration, expected in 1Q2027, will show whether rolled earnings and restated cash generation convert into a distribution [S0, S15]. The Aceh IUP renewal window in 2027 is the next permitting checkpoint [S5, S8].

Between updates we monitor GEMS's share price and dividend first, because the associate is the largest part of the SOTP [S12]; the holdco discount to pre-discount NAV second, because a sustained narrowing or widening is the thesis [S0]; then contractor overburden volume and coal getting, services EBITDA, the related-party revenue share and the fuel book [S12, S4]. Finally, net debt to EBITDA, registry free float and the GEMS stake move the valuation before any disclosure [S5, S13].

base.narrative: The parts are marked at what the market and the comps say they are worth: GEMS at its listed market price, the operating segments on the LTM to 30 September 2026 net of SG&A at comp-supported multiples, MDB at the only observable transaction value, PJU at acquisition fair value and parent overhead at ten times; the holdco discount persists at the level the market applies to the corrected NAV, the most-likely branch of the house archetype, which puts narrowing at about one-third over three years. No narrowing is assumed.

bear.narrative: The drawdown the section leads with is in the table, not outside it: the holdco discount widens ten points as the correlated governance and coal risks bite, and the GEMS mark is de-rated twenty per cent — the "fifth off the mark" the prior report sized but did not count. Because the engine cannot re-price a fixed market mark, the GEMS hit is mapped into the discount lever: the residual (1 − discount) is re-priced as (1 − base discount − 0.10) × (1 − GEMS/NAV × 0.20), so the discount widens from the base level to 81.26%, which is +12.371 points, not +10. A thermal-coal fall also hits the contractor's GEMS-controlled revenue block, so the same driver is not counted twice; a repeat related-party transfer at or below the MDB transaction mark (the mark is already at the observable price) is a further governance downside stated but not modelled. Mirrored with the bull on both drivers.

bull.narrative: The mirror of the bear: the discount narrows ten points as the PJU first cut lands at end-2026, NCN keeps ramping and the FY2026 dividend upstream rises, with the free-float step closed by 31 March 2027, and the GEMS mark re-rates twenty per cent with the coal complex. The GEMS re-rating is mapped into the discount lever in the same way, giving −14.613 points. The PJU reserve base (34.06 Mt at GAR 4,600-5,000, S8) is the operating option: a mine plan would capitalise it above the acquisition fair value, but no plan is disclosed and the base does not invent one. Mirrored with the bear on both drivers.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: ROLLED TO THE LATEST TWELVE MONTHS. LTM revenue to 30 September 2026 is US$1,075.05m against FY2025's US$1,038.17m, a 3.55% increase (S15/F67, S12); 9M2026 revenue was 4.7% higher year on year and the company attributes the recovery to the mining-contractor business and expects the dry-season conditions to persist (S16). No separate revenue plan is disclosed, so FY2027E onward is held flat at the new run-rate rather than extrapolating the third-quarter peak.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs (LTM to 30 September 2026)
assumptions.basis: HELD AT THE LTM MARGIN, correctly labelled. LTM gross profit is US$140.67m on LTM revenue US$1,075.05m, a 13.085% margin; 9M2026 itself is 12.0% (US$98.295172m on US$818.525199m, F68/F67) against 7.8% in 9M2025 (S15, S16). The LTM is the last actual and the most-likely anchor; the improvement is sourced (lower rainfall hours, higher overburden removal and coal getting, lower cost-to-revenue ratio, S16) and the base does not extrapolate a further improvement. The prior label said "9M2026 run-rate" for a 13.085% figure; that was wrong and is corrected here. The 3.91-point gap between the input-implied model margin and the audited FY2025A actual is the sourced LTM margin roll, recorded in qc_justifications.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue (LTM recurring, excluding the one-off credit-loss provision)
assumptions.basis: HELD AT THE LTM RECURRING RATIO. LTM selling and distribution US$1.966441m plus LTM general and administrative US$64.245311m is US$66.211752m; removing the expected-credit-loss provision step of US$11.788934m (9M2026 US$11.990192m, F90, against US$0.201258m in 9M2025) leaves US$54.422818m on LTM revenue US$1,075.05m = 5.062%. The provision is a receivables write-down, not an operating cost, and it more than doubled the reported G&A run-rate; charging it forever would understate the earnings power and charging it never would ignore a real credit cost, so the prior-year base provision is retained inside the 5.062%. The previous 6.202% was the reported LTM ratio including the provision, mislabelled as the 9M2026 ratio (9M2026 is 6.04% including the provision). Professional fees are carved out of the segment marks and charged at ten times at holdco level; they remain in this consolidated ratio.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: RESTATED FROM THE AUDITED NOTES. FY2025 total depreciation and amortisation was US$211.565247m (F17) over revenue US$1,038.170254m = 20.379%. The data pack carried only US$6.83m because it reads the G&A depreciation line of a direct-method filer; the audited segment note shows the charge is split across cost of revenue, services and mining properties. The fact restates FY2024 too (F18, US$205.078832m) so the history is consistent and the engine rebuilds EBITDA from it.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: HELD AT THE LAST ACTUAL. FY2025 cash-flow capital expenditure was US$136.575725m (the pack's capex, which reconciles to fixed-asset additions plus payables for fixed assets in the audited cash-flow statement, S12) over revenue US$1,038.17m = 13.155%. The segment note's US$195.6m includes the timing of payables and the PJU acquisition, so it is not the sustaining rate. Management reports a "stricter capital expenditure discipline" in 1Q26 (S3); the base does not bank a further cut without a full-year source.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue)) = 10.67%

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: LAST ACTUAL, not the four-year average. LTM income tax is US$18.91m against LTM profit before income tax of US$149.87m, a 12.6% effective rate: 9M2026 income tax of US$13.685237m plus final tax of US$0.649115m on PBT of US$116.404821m is 12.3% (S15), and the trailing twelve months bring in the higher FY2025 charge (S12). The base uses the rate the LK is actually paying.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance charges of US$76.554485m over opening debt of US$976.329m is 7.84%; 1H2026 finance charges of US$31.350318m annualised over opening debt of US$969.108m is 6.47% (S5). The December 2025 Rp4.2tn syndicated facility (F22/S10) refinanced part of the book at a lower rate, so the base uses 7.5%, between the two observed rates and below the engine's stale four-year average of 9.9%.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income of US$4.382377m over opening cash of US$170.318m is 2.57%; 1H2026 finance income of US$2.101988m annualised over opening cash of US$202.369m is 2.08% (S5). The base uses 2.0%, the current run-rate.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No sourced new borrowing. The Rp4.2tn syndicated facility signed in December 2025 refinances existing debt rather than adding to it (S10/F22), and the 30 September 2026 balance sheet shows debt falling to US$872.3m from US$969.1m at FY2025 (S15). Held at zero.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items (associate income plus other income)
assumptions.basis: ROLLED TO THE 9M2026 ACTUAL. The corporate template has no separate associate line. LTM PBT is US$149.874m (FY2025 US$75.860m less 9M2025 US$42.392m plus 9M2026 US$116.405m, S15/F71/S12); the restated operating line is anchored on the same LTM P&L and the balancing non-operating stream is US$144.504m after the engine's finance charge and finance income. It is anchored on the 9M2026 share of associates of US$97.494m (F70) and other income net of US$30.651m (F76), both up sharply on 9M2025, and includes a US$15.797m one-off loss on disposal of investment (F78) that depresses rather than flatters the LTM figure. Held flat at the new run-rate, per the most-likely card.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2025 minority interest was a US$0.136m loss and the minority balance sheet line is only US$6.121m at 30 September 2026 against equity of US$956.962m (F73, F74), so the minority share of group profit is immaterial; the base sets it to zero rather than the engine's 2.7% four-year average, which is distorted by the pre-2024 NCN/PJU structure.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 DPS of Rp97 (US$0.005445) over EPS of US$0.02565 is 21.2% (S0/S12); the per-share dividend has fallen for four years as coal earnings fell. The base holds the last actual payout rather than the engine's four-year average or a recovery, both of which would be unsourced.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: engine default constant: no buyback, rights issue or share plan is disclosed in the FY2025 audited statements or the 9M2026 LK

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set to 0.0: the holdco_sotp method set has no DCF, so no method consumes a terminal growth rate. The input is set to zero for cross-name consistency with the sister holdco names rather than left at the engine's 2% default.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: BASE AT THE DISCOUNT THE MARKET APPLIES TO THE CORRECTED NAV — PERSISTENCE, THE MOST-LIKELY BRANCH OF THE HOUSE BASE RATE. (i) The holdco-discount-narrowing archetype in data/base_rates.yaml puts the probability of the discount narrowing at 0.33 over three years (up-case +28%, down-case -18%), so the most probable single path is persistence: about two-thirds of the distribution does not narrow. (ii) The number is now an observation against the corrected 30 September net debt, the transaction-implied MDB mark and the LTM segment marks: the price of Rp2,540 is 68.9% below the corrected pre-discount NAV of Rp8,164/share, and the base holds that level. It is not solved from the price to preserve a prior output; it is the level the market is in fact applying, disclosed as such, and the base assumes no narrowing. (iii) It is far above the peer modal 0.30 (ADRO, BRPT, CUAN, DSSA, TOBA at 0.30; ASII 0.25) and above the closest peer IMJS at 0.60; the gap is governance and structure — thin float (14.97%, S0), family control (F55), related-party revenue 59.14% (F52), and the MDB stake transferred below carrying to a related party (F38/F54). The warrant therefore sits at the wide end, and the base rates persistence there. The narrowing is the BULL case: the PJU first cut targeted for end-2026, the FY2026 dividend upstream declared in the first quarter of 2027, and the IDX free-float step (15% by 31 March 2027, S13) are the dated events, and none is assumed in the base. Bear: discount widens ten points AND a twenty per cent GEMS de-rating, mapped into 12.371 points because the engine cannot re-price the fixed market mark; bull: the mirrored narrowing and GEMS re-rating, mapped into -14.613 points. See scenarios.

challenges.challenge: The 60/25/15 blend makes the base assume a discount narrowing it says it does not assume, and that is what carries the BUY. SOTP Rp2,497 = pre-discount NAV Rp7,398.7/share x (1 - 66.2462%). The P/E leg Rp3,247 (3.774x own five-year average on LTM np_parent US$130.55m) implies a 56.1% discount; the P/BV leg Rp4,861 (0.776x on US$950.84m book) implies a 34.3%; the weighted effective discount is 0.6 x 66.25 + 0.25 x 56.1 + 0.15 x 34.3 = 58.9%, i.e. the base has already banked 7.3 points of the 10-point narrowing assigned to the bull (56.2%). Even the bear's blended value Rp2,595 implies a 64.9% effective discount, narrower than the stated 66.2% base. At today's spot multiples (P/E 2.95x, P/B 0.41x) both cross-checks equal the Rp2,540 price, the blend is Rp2,514 and the target Rp2,558 — a 7.9% total return, HOLD, not 30.3%. The report discloses the divergence but resolves it in the wrong direction; the "30% above SOTP" headline is an artefact of comparing undiscounted cross-checks to a 66%-discounted SOTP (against the pre-discount NAV the P/E is 56% below, not above).
challenges.answer: The P/E and P/BV legs are dropped entirely, not down-weighted: weights are now SOTP 1.0, P/E 0.0, P/BV 0.0, so there is no blend and no embedded narrowing. The base applies one discount, the market-implied 68.89%, to the corrected NAV; the report prints that level, states that the SOTP leg is therefore a market mark, and discloses the old divergence (undiscounted cross-checks compared with a discounted SOTP). Spot multiples are shown only as a check and, on a comparable basis, equal the price, so they support no higher target. Target and rating are restated from the engine: Rp2,621, ADD, TR 11.0%.

challenges.challenge: The SOTP deducts the 30 June 2026 net debt of US$705.324m (S5: debt US$922.343m less cash US$217.019m) although the 30 September LK and the pack put net debt at US$649.2m (S15/F75; S0), US$56.1m lower — about Rp365/share of pre-discount NAV. The stated reason ("we keep the June debt because the base discount is solved from the price") is circular: it makes the SOTP output a mirror of the price, so the 60%-weighted primary method carries no independent valuation. It is also arithmetically wrong on its own terms: the input discount 66.2462% is not the market-implied discount, which the report itself prints as 65.7%, and the SOTP Rp2,497 is 1.7% below the Rp2,540 price. The card requires the LK's net debt, and the MOST_LIKELY card requires the latest balance sheet.
challenges.answer: The SOTP now bridges to the 30 September 2026 LK: bank loans, current maturities, other long-term loans and leases less cash, with the 30 September NCI deducted separately. The 30 June debt and the price-solve rationale are gone. Because the discount is explicitly the market-implied level, the report states that the SOTP leg is a market mark and that the independent content is the NAV and the scenario distribution; no claim of a target above the price is made on the SOTP alone.

challenges.challenge: GEMS is US$695.570m, 61.9% of the US$1,122.9m pre-discount NAV, and the scenarios shock only a.holdco_discount (+/-10 points), so GEMS and every operating mark are identical in base, bear and bull. A 20% GEMS de-rating — the report's own "fifth off the mark" — is US$139.1m, 12.4% of NAV (~Rp918/share pre-discount), larger than the bear's 10-point discount move (Rp740/share), and would take the bear below the Rp2,540 price. The bear therefore ends at Rp2,939 (+15.7%) and the 25% bear contributes no downside to the probability-weighted target, which equals the base. The report calls the GEMS mark its #1 risk and then gives it zero scenario weight.
challenges.answer: The engine cannot re-price a holdings mark inside a scenario, so the 20% GEMS de-rating is mapped into the discount lever at the equivalent NAV effect and mirrored in the bull. The bear now combines the 10-point widening with that mapped de-rating and ends below the price; the bull mirrors it. The report says in terms that the probability-weighted target now includes the GEMS risk and that the mapped shock, not a direct mark, is the mechanism. The bear probability is kept at 0.25 because the bear now contains the section's lead risk.

challenges.challenge: MDB is carried at US$82.533m audited book (F37, 40% stake at 30 June 2026), but the only observable transaction is the April 2026 transfer of a 10% stake to related party PT Inti Murni Kencana for US$10.0m (F38/F54): that values 100% of MDB at US$100m and the remaining 40% at US$40m, about half the book mark. The disposal loss of US$15.797m (F78) is the same transaction — 10% of the 50% carrying value (US$127.429m x 0.2 = US$25.486m) sold for US$10.0m. The assumptions say the transfer "implies a lower value than carrying, so the audited book value is the defensible mark", which is backwards: the observable price is the mark's upper bound, not evidence for it. The overstatement is ~US$42.5m (~Rp275/share pre-discount) and the bear contains no repeat related-party transfer.
challenges.answer: MDB is now marked at US$40.0m, four times the US$10.0m paid for the 10% stake and therefore the transaction-implied value of the remaining 40%; the US$82.533m book and the "book is defensible" language are removed. The US$42.5m difference is quantified in the NAV. A repeat related-party transfer is stated in the bear narrative rather than modelled as a separate shock, because MDB already sits at the observable transaction price and a correlated contractor repricing is carried by the bear's discount widening; adding another discount leg would double-count the same governance risk.

challenges.challenge: The report and assumptions state that PJU has "no reserve or production plan ... disclosed in the archived record" and carry it at US$56.256m of sourced mining-property capex. S8 contradicts that: p.516 (note on subsidiaries) gives PJU total reserves 34.06 Mt and remaining reserves 34.06 Mt at 31 December 2025 (based on a PT NRM Konsultan Indonesia report dated 30 June 2024), with the IUP valid to 2032 and extendable twice by 20 years; p.159 gives GAR 4,600-5,000 kcal/kg and the 4,800-ha concession. The carried value is US$1.65/t of reserves, and the bull narrative gives the PJU first cut no value at all. The MOST_LIKELY card requires a development project to be worth at least sunk capex; it does not require it to be capped there when reserves are disclosed.
challenges.answer: The "no reserve or production plan is disclosed" statement is deleted and replaced with the sourced position: S8 p.516 discloses 34.06 Mt of total and remaining reserves for PJU, S8 p.159 gives the GAR 4,600-5,000 range and the 4,800-ha concession, and the IUP runs to 28 December 2032. The report now states both PJU's and NCN's reserves. PJU remains at the US$56.256m acquisition fair value, with the reason sourced rather than assumed: the group's own NCN acquisition was US$14.0m for 31.00 Mt (about US$0.45/t), so PJU's US$1.65/t is at the top of the group's own transaction range for a 2011-2012-vintage estimate with no mine plan. The reserve-based upside is assigned to the bull rather than capitalised in the base.

challenges.challenge: The operating marks are struck on FY2025 net segment EBITDA (consolidated US$254.22m) while the base forecast and the P/E leg use the LTM run-rate (US$293.08m operating EBITDA; the company's LTM adjusted EBITDA is US$399.9m, +42.4%, F81). 9M2026 revenue rose 4.7% and the gross margin to 12.0% from 7.8% (F67/F68/F82, S16), and the report itself says the improvement is sourced (drier weather, higher overburden and coal getting, lower cost-to-revenue). Marking the parts on the older year is an unjustified conservatism inconsistent with the base's own "last actual" anchor; at 4.0x the US$38.9m gap is ~US$156m of NAV (about Rp1,010/share pre-discount, ~Rp225 on the target after the discount and weights). The assumptions also claim NCN's 1H2026 0.4 Mt (F12) is "inside this EBITDA", which is impossible for a FY2025 figure.
challenges.answer: All four operating marks are now struck on the LTM to 30 September 2026: segment EBITDA is the FY2025 audited column less the 9M2025 comparative plus the 9M2026 actual, recurring SG&A (excluding the one-off ECL provision and parent professional fees) is allocated pro rata to external revenue, and the resulting marks replace the FY2025 strike. The NCN claim is corrected: its 1H2026 volumes are not "inside this EBITDA"; the LTM construction is what captures them. The report states the method and the reason (the last actual is the most-likely anchor).

challenges.challenge: gross_margin is labelled "held at the 9M2026 run-rate" but is the LTM 13.085% (9M2026 itself is 12.0%, F68/F67); opex_pct 6.202% is the LTM ratio while the 9M2026 ratio is 6.04% (49.43/818.53). The FY2026E EBITDA margin of 27.3% is therefore 2.8pp above FY2025A's 24.5%, and the QC calibration reports FY2025A actual 24.49% versus input-implied 27.26% (gap 2.77pp) with qc_justifications empty. The LTM roll is a defensible sourced drift, but it is not labelled or justified as one.
challenges.answer: The labels are corrected: gross_margin is described as the LTM ratio and opex_pct as the LTM recurring ratio (5.0623%), explicitly excluding the one-off expected-credit-loss provision while retaining the prior-year base charge. The report states the 9M2026 gross margin separately and no longer calls the LTM figure a 9M2026 run-rate. The calibration drift is recorded in qc_justifications with S16.

challenges.challenge: The update runs 5,160 words against the house 500-3,500 update range (fund record lint emits the warning), and the summary, section 3 and section 4 repeat the same SOTP/cross-check argument three times. The length is not neutral: the repetition asserts the "parts worth more" conclusion without adding evidence, and the report already has an eight-section structure that carries the argument.
challenges.answer: The report is cut from about 5,160 words to 3,500, with the valuation reasoning stated once: the duplicated SOTP/cross-check paragraphs in the investment summary and section 4 are removed, section 5 repeats the scenario mechanics only where it adds the risk case, and the remaining sourced arguments and the single statement of cross-check divergence are kept.

challenges.challenge: VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT §1 requires "minus holdco opex capitalized at ~10x". The SOTP charges the full consolidated SG&A and other operating expenses (US$61.024m) inside the segment marks at 3.5-4.0x and adds no separate bridge line, so the parent-level corporate cost is capitalised at the segment multiple rather than ~10x; if any material part of the US$61.0m is parent-level rather than segment-level selling and administration, the charge is understated (US$61.0m at 4x is US$244m versus US$610m at 10x). The analyst's no-double-count rationale is sound for the segment cost but does not isolate the parent component the card names.
challenges.answer: Parent-level cost is now isolated and charged separately. Professional fees are the identifiable corporate, listing, audit, legal and treasury block in the consolidated G&A schedule; their LTM value is capitalised at ten times and deducted as its own holding line, and the segment marks exclude professional fees so the same cost is not multiplied again at segment level. Segment SG&A stays inside the marks. holdco_opex_note documents the split.

missing_bull_case.note: PJU is carried at US$56.3m sunk capex with the statement that "no reserve or production plan is disclosed", but S8 p.516 discloses 34.06 Mt of total and remaining reserves and S8 p.159 gives GAR 4,600-5,000 kcal/kg; that is US$1.65/t for a 4,800-ha deposit with an IUP to 2032 and two 20-year extensions, and the bull gets no credit. The operating marks (US$1,000.2m, 89% of gross SOTP value) use FY2025 segment EBITDA (US$254.2m) while the forecast and P/E leg use the LTM run-rate (US$293.1m; company LTM adjusted EBITDA US$399.9m, +42.4%, F81), and the claim that NCN's 1H2026 volumes (F12) are "inside this EBITDA" is impossible for a FY2025 figure. The bull moves only the discount, so neither the PJU first cut nor the 9M2026 recovery reaches value. C5, C6.

response.note: PJU and NCN reserves are disclosed and cited; the operating marks use the LTM to 30 September 2026 rather than FY2025; and the bull carries the GEMS re-rating and the reserve upside. See C5 and C6.
response.evidence: F83/F84 reserves (S8 p.516), F91/F92 calorific grades (S8 p.159); LTM segment marks from S12/S15; engine ok.

missing_bear_case.note: GEMS is US$695.6m, 61.9% of pre-discount NAV, and is held at market in every scenario; the 25% bear moves only the discount 10 points, so the report's own #1 risk carries zero probability weight and the bear is still +15.7% above the price. A 20% GEMS de-rating (the report's "fifth off the mark") cuts pre-discount NAV 12.4% (~Rp918/share), larger than the bear's 10-point move. MDB is carried at US$82.5m book while the April 2026 10% transfer for US$10.0m implies US$40m for the remaining 40% — roughly half the mark — and repeat related-party leakage is not in the bear even though the report calls related-party gravity the modal IDX value-destruction channel. C3, C4.

response.note: The bear now contains a mapped 20% GEMS de-rating and ends below the price, and MDB is marked at the transaction-implied US$40.0m rather than book. A repeat related-party transfer remains a stated bear factor rather than a separate modelled shock, because MDB is already at the observable price. See C3 and C4.

assumption_realism.note: The GEMS market mark is verifiable and correct. The discount is not the "same" market-implied level it claims (65.7% is printed; 66.246% is input, so SOTP Rp2,497 sits 1.7% below the Rp2,540 price). The segment multiples (4.0x/4.0x/3.5x/2.0x) are struck on FY2025 net segment EBITDA and benchmarked to coal producers (GEMS 4.7x, AADI 4.6x, BSSR 6.4x, ITMG 2.7x, ADRO 8.0x) rather than mining-services peers, and are applied to an earnings year the 9M2026 actuals have already beaten. gross_margin is labelled the 9M2026 run-rate but is the LTM 13.085% (9M2026 is 12.0%, F68/F67) and opex is 6.202% versus the 9M2026 6.04% (49.43/818.53). C1, C2, C6, C7.

response.note: The discount is now the market-implied level and the P/E and P/BV legs are gone, so there is no blended narrowing. Segment marks are LTM, the NCN claim is corrected, and the margin labels match the LTM ratios actually used. See C1, C2, C6 and C7.
response.evidence: weights 1.0/0/0; holdco_discount 0.688892 = reverse-solve implied; gross_margin 0.13085 LTM; opex 0.050623 recurring; engine ok.

evidence_and_citations.note: Most facts are sound and the D&A restatement is properly traced to F17/F18 and the segment columns. Three load-bearing statements fail their sources. "No reserve or production plan is disclosed" is contradicted by S8 p.516 (34.06 Mt) and p.159 (GAR 4,600-5,000). "The base applies the same 66.2%" is contradicted by the report's own 65.7% implied discount. The MDB transfer loss is F78's US$15.797m, but the report treats the same transaction as evidence that book is "the defensible mark" rather than as the mark's upper bound. C2, C4, C5.

response.note: All three load-bearing statements are corrected: the reserve statement now cites S8 pp.159/516; the base prints one discount, the market-implied 68.89%, rather than claiming a same-as-implied 66.2%; and the MDB transaction is used as the mark's observable upper bound, not as evidence for book. See C2, C4 and C5.
response.evidence: F83, F84, F91, F92 verified (fund record facts PASS); reverse-solve 0.688892; MDB 40.0 versus F37 82.533.

valuation_method_fit.note: The holdco card is the right frame and GEMS at market, MDB at book and PJU at sourced capex are the card's marks, but the 60/25/15 blend is not internally consistent. The P/E leg (3.77x own five-year average) implies a 56.1% discount to NAV; the P/BV leg (0.78x) implies a 34.3% discount; weighted with the 66.2% SOTP the base's effective discount is 58.9% — 7.3 points inside the persistence case and about 73% of the bull's 10-point narrowing. At today's spot multiples (~2.95x P/E, ~0.41x P/BV) both cross-checks equal the price and the target is ~Rp2,558 (HOLD), so the BUY is carried by the re-rating embedded in the 5y-average multiples. Keeping the 30 June net debt (US$705.3m vs US$649.2m at 30 September) to preserve the price-solved discount makes the SOTP a mirror rather than an estimate; the card's ~10x holdco opex line is also not applied (consolidated SG&A is charged at segment multiples). C1, C2, C9.

response.note: The blend is removed (SOTP-only), the bridge is dated 30 September 2026, and parent overhead is a separate ten-times line. The single-method choice is the direct remedy the FATAL demanded and is disclosed as such. See C1, C2 and C9.
response.evidence: weights {sotp 1.0, pe 0.0, pbv 0.0}; holdco_net_debt 652.025541; parent overhead -84.584640; engine ADD, tp 2621.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose says "the narrowing is the bull case, not the base", yet the blend banks ~7.3 points of narrowing and 40% of the weight sits on multiples that are 26% (P/E) and 91% (P/BV) above today's price. The conclusion does not survive the re-rating assumption being removed: spot multiples give a ~7.9% total return, not a 30.3% return. The bear is a positive-return bear (+15.7%) and the probability-weighted target equals the base by construction, so the scenarios flatter the downside. C1, C3.

response.note: The proven re-rating is eliminated: the base applies the market-implied discount and 40% of the weight no longer sits on five-year-average multiples. The bear now contains the GEMS de-rating and ends below the price, so it is a downside, not a positive-return bear. See C1 and C3.
response.evidence: weights 1.0/0/0; bear tp 1642.53 versus price 2540; base tp 2857.67; weighted 2912.73; final 2621 after 10% liquidity.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The V5.2a holdco reframe is applied consistently and the retired coal-producer frame (life-of-asset DCF, 0.28 realisation) is not smuggled back. GEMS is marked at the listed price, the group reports in dollars and the macro spot USD/IDR is used (with the FY2027E disclosed as the alternative), and thermal coal is NEUTRAL in the macro deck, so no deck variable is misread. The remaining mismatch — contractor multiples benchmarked to coal producers rather than mining-services peers — is an assumption issue recorded under assumption_realism, not a deck inconsistency.
